questions.question: Day 16 Practice (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)): When talking about giving street directions (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My manager'?

options.a: Signal crossing left turn take. yesterday
options.b: Signal crossing left turn take.
options.c: I am giving street directions right now.
options.d: Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.".

questions.question: Day 16 Vocabulary (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'touch base'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Briefly connect with someone to exchange news.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'touch base' means: briefly connect with someone to exchange news. Example: "I will touch base with you after the review."

questions.question: Day 16 Vocabulary (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'hedge against'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: Protect against potential financial or operational loss.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'hedge against' means: protect against potential financial or operational loss. Example: "We must diversify to hedge against market risk."

questions.question:
Day 16 Translation Scenario 1 (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.c: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 16 Translation Scenario 2 (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: Your thought good but budget not allow.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.
options.d: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 16 Translation Scenario 3 (Phone Calls & Deliveries (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.c: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.
